# Data description

## Data Source

The data used in this exercise was taken from: A experiment run in the TerraX Cube hypobaric chambers in Bolzano, IT in November 2025 on *Arabidopsis thaliana* individuals. Data collected by Marta De Giuli, Bouchra El Omari, and Emily Mason and compiled by Marta De Giuli in 2026.

## Description of the data

Description of the data and the question(s).

-   4 chambers for a 2 factorial design :
    -   2 pairs at the same elevation/pressure
    -   2 pairs at the same D/pressure corrected VPD
-   In each chamber we have 30 pots each containing 3-4 individuals, kept at 100% soil saturation.
-   We have a total of 120 pots across all chambers.
-   We have temporal data for some measures - taken halfway through the experiment and taken at the end, while other measures only have one temporal point taken at the end of the two week experimental conditions.
-   Our main goal is to understand *how* or *if* pressure modulates ecophysiological parameters of *Arabidopsis thaliana* and how pressure interracts with humidity. The goal of this is to disentangle the effect of pressure and humidity to better understand the stressors high alpine plants are subjected to.

Covariates:

-   Biometric measurements including:

    -   plant height, rosette diameter and leaf number
    -   fresh weight, turgid weight, dry weight, and calculated RWC

-   Photosynthetic measurements, as taken with a WALZ device:

    -   Net carbon assimilation, gas exchange (stomatal conductance), evapotranspiration
    -   and calculated: Ci:Ca

-   Chlorophyll fluorescence measurements, as taken with a FluorCAM 600 from leaf discs:

    -   Y(II), NPQ, 1-qL

-   Metabolitic measurements

    -   C:N ratios, d13C values

    -   chlorophyll content, carotene content, chlorophyll a:b ratio

```{r}
#| label: Functions
#| include: false
#create function for calculation of standard deviation, standard error, 95% confidence interval
summarySE <- function(data=NULL, measurevar, groupvars=NULL, na.rm=FALSE,
                      conf.interval=.95, .drop=TRUE) {
  library(plyr)
  
  # New version of length which can handle NA's: if na.rm==T, don't count them
  length2 <- function (x, na.rm=FALSE) {
    if (na.rm) sum(!is.na(x))
    else       length(x)
  }
  
  # This does the summary. For each group's data frame, return a vector with
  # N, mean, and sd
  datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
                 .fun = function(xx, col) {
                   c(N    = length2(xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     sd   = sd     (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm)
                   )
                 },
                 measurevar
  )
  
  # Rename the "mean" column    
  datac <- rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))
  
  datac$se <- datac$sd / sqrt(datac$N)  # Calculate standard error of the mean
  
  # Confidence interval multiplier for standard error
  # Calculate t-statistic for confidence interval: 
  # e.g., if conf.interval is .95, use .975 (above/below), and use df=N-1
  ciMult <- qt(conf.interval/2 + .5, datac$N-1)
  datac$ci <- datac$se * ciMult
  
  return(datac)
}

# Self-starting function for the exponential decay model
SSexpDecay <- selfStart(
  model = ~ Pmin + Pmax * exp(-alpha * I / Pmax),
  initial = function(mCall, data, LHS, ...) {
    # Extract the independent variable and the response variable
    xy <- sortedXyData(mCall[["I"]], LHS, data)
    
    # Ensure there are enough data points
    if (nrow(xy) < 4) stop("bro you don't have enough values")
    
    #extract indep + response variables
    I <- xy[["x"]]
    y <- xy[["y"]]
    
    # Initial guess for Pmax is the maximum observed value of y
    Pmax_init <- max(y)
    Pmin_init <- min(y)
    
    # Fit a linear model to the log-transformed data to estimate alpha
    # Avoid log(0) by replacing 0s with a small positive value
    y_transformed <- ifelse(y == 0, 1e-6, y)
    log_y <- log(y_transformed)
    
    # Linear model: log(y) =log(Pmin)+ log(Pmax) - (alpha / Pmax) * I
    fit <- lm(log_y ~ I)
    alpha_init <- -coef(fit)[2] * Pmax_init  # Extract alpha from the slope
    
    # Return the initial parameter estimates as a named list
    setNames(c(Pmax = Pmax_init, alpha = alpha_init, Pmin = Pmin_init), 
             mCall[c("Pmax", "alpha", "Pmin")])
  },
  parameters = c("Pmax", "alpha", "Pmin")
)

# Function to create compact letter displays
create_cld <- function(subset_data) {
  # Extract group comparisons and p-values
  comparisons <- strsplit(as.character(subset_data$pairs), "-")       #extract pairs
  groups <- unique(unlist(comparisons))                               #extract unique treatments
  p_matrix <- matrix(1, nrow = length(groups), ncol = length(groups)) #create square matrix with for treatment comparisons
  #rename the rows and columns to treatment names
  rownames(p_matrix) <- groups
  colnames(p_matrix) <- groups
  
  #for each comparison (saved in 'comparisons'), save p-value in matrix)
  for (i in 1:nrow(subset_data)) {
    pair <- comparisons[[i]]
    p_matrix[pair[1], pair[2]] <- subset_data$p_value[i]
    p_matrix[pair[2], pair[1]] <- subset_data$p_value[i]
  }
  
  # Create compact letter display
  cld <- multcompLetters(p_matrix)
  return(cld$Letters)
}

# Function to check overlap between two confidence intervals
check_overlap <- function(ci1, ci2) {
  !(ci1[2] < ci2[1] | ci2[2] < ci1[1])
}

# Pairwise comparison of confidence intervals
compare_param <- function(data) {
  comparisons <- data.frame(
    pair = character(),
    overlap = logical(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (i in 1:(nrow(data) - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):nrow(data)) {
      pair_name <- paste(data$treatment[i], data$treatment[j], sep = "-")
      overlap <- check_overlap(
        ci1 = c(data$low[i], data$high[i]),
        ci2 = c(data$low[j], data$high[j])
      )
      comparisons <- rbind(comparisons, data.frame(pair = pair_name, overlap = overlap))
    }
  }
  
  return(comparisons)
}

# Compare coefficients of non-nested models as per Clogg et al. (1995) formula
# returns a data.frame with the diff, zdiff, and p.value of each coefficient

compare_coefs <- function(.data1, .data2){
  
  # imports map_dbl() and pluck() functions from purrr library
  import::here(map_dbl, pluck, .from = purrr)  
  
  # extract the relevant data
  b1 = map_dbl(df1[, 1], pluck)     #get reg. coefs for model 1
  se1 = map_dbl(df1[, 2], pluck)    #get std errors for model 1
  
  b2 = map_dbl(df2[, 1], pluck)     #get reg. coefs for model 2
  se2 = map_dbl(df2[, 2], pluck)    #get std. errors for model 2
  
  # Clogg et al. (1995) formula as cited by Ray Paternoster et al. (1998)
  b = b1 - b2
  s1 = se1^2
  s2 = se2^2
  sc = s1 + s2
  v = b / sqrt(sc)
  
  data.frame(diff=b, zdiff=v, `p-value`=format(2*pnorm(-abs(v)), scientific=FALSE))
  
}
```

```{r}
## PAM data ----

################
# #Note: PAM parameters are defined as the following:
# F0	                              Minimal chlorophyll fluorescence intensity measured in the dark-adapted state, when all PSII reaction centres are open
# F	                                Average of Ft in 3 s , when a SP is triggered
# Fm	                              Maximal chlorophyll fluorescence intensity measured in the dark-adapted state during the application of a saturating pulse of light
# Fm'	                              Maximal chlorophyll fluorescence intensity measured in the light-adapted state during the application of a saturating pulse of light
# Fv/Fm	                            Maximum quantum yield of PSII photochemistry measured in the dark-adapted state
# Y(II)= (Fm'− Fs)/Fm'	            Effective quantum yield of photochemical energy conversion in PSII
# NPQ=(Fm − Fm')/Fm'	              Stern-Volmer non-photochemical quenching coefficient
# qP=(Fm'− Fs)/(Fm'− F0′)	          Coefficient of photochemical quenching of variable fluorescence based on the puddle model of PSII
# qN=(Fm − Fm')/(Fm'−F0′)	          Coefficient of non-photochemical quenching of variable fluorescence
# qL = qP × F0/Fs	                  Coefficient of photochemical quenching of variable fluorescence based on the lake model of PSII
# Y(NO) = 1/(PNQ + 1 + qL(Fm/F0-1))	Quantum yield of non-regulated energy dissipation in PSII
# Y(NPQ) = 1-Y(II)-Y(NO)	          Quantum yield of regulated energy dissipation in PSII
#
################

pam <- read_csv("../RAW Data/PAM.csv") |>
  mutate(treatment = substr(sample,5,9),
         D         = as.numeric(substr(treatment, 4, 5)),
         pressure  = case_when(
           substr(treatment, 1, 2) == 26 ~ 98,
           substr(treatment, 1, 2) == 40 ~ 61),
         drought   = case_when(
           time == "T2" & substr(ID,3,3) == "d" ~ "d",
           .default = "nd"
         )
         )
```

### Chlorophyll A:B

Here we look at the chlorophyll A:B ratio. First testing for normality within the dataset and then proceeding with the graphing.

```{r}
#| label: chlorophyll a:b
#| echo: false
#check for normality
shapiro.test(pigments$chlab) 
#p-value = 0.3652 and thus > than 0.05 so the data is normally distributed

cat(paste("Since the p-value is", 
      ifelse(shapiro.test(pigments$chlab)$p.value > 0.05, "non-significant,", "significant,"), 
      "the data is", 
      ifelse(shapiro.test(pigments$chlab)$p.value > 0.05, "normally distributed \n and we will use t-test for comparison going forward.", 
             "non-normally distributed \n and we will use the Wilcox test for comparison going forward.")))

chlab.plot<-
  pigments.comp |>
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = chlab, fill = treatment))+
  geom_boxplot(data = pigments, color = "grey",fill = "grey")+ 
  geom_boxplot()+
  geom_jitter(width=0.01)+
  labs(title = "Chlorophyll A:B",
       x = NULL,
       y = "A : B")+
  scale_fill_manual(values= cols)+
  stat_compare_means(method = method2, 
                     label = "p.signif",
                     label.y = 3.05,
                     label.x = c(2, 3, 3.5, 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 1)
  )+
  stat_compare_means(method = method2, 
                     label = "p.format",
                     label.y.npc = "bottom"
  )+
  facet_grid(time~comparison, drop = TRUE)+
  ylim(NA, 3.1)+
  theme_bw( )+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom")

#final chlorophyll A/B plot
chlab.plot

# #saveplot
# ggsave("./D Gradient Figures/chlab.plot.png", 
#        chlab.plot,  
#        width = 2418, 
#        height = 1756, 
#        units = "px")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false
#####
# Note: If we compare estimates of the same coeffs from samples of different 
# populations, we can indicate statistical significance if CIs don't overlap, 
# but not robustly say that there is no difference if they do.
#####

#looking at some significance

#A Note: We cannot compare individual models pairwise with an ANOVA as it abuses
#the assumption of the F-test that they are nested and fitted to the same data.
#THUS we will compare the model fitted to the _whole_ data set compared to the
#same model fitted for each group to see if there is a statistical difference
#between groups. If this returns positive, we will look at the alpha parameter
#individually - the one defining the shape of the curve, using the CI interval
#generated by nls().

#convert treatments to factors
pam.factor <- pam.comp %>% mutate(treatment = as.factor(treatment))

#create frames to fill in for loop with ci overlaps
psii.overlap <- data.frame(pair = character(),
                           overlap = logical(),
                           time = character())

psii.cld <- data.frame(treatment = character(),
                       comparison = character(),
                       letter = character(),
                       time = character())

#initiate data frame to store parameter value and confidence intervals
psii.alpha <- data.frame(treatment = character(),
                         est = numeric(),
                         low = numeric(),
                         high = numeric(),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

for(comp in unique(pam.comp$comparison)){
  subset <- pam.factor |>
    filter(comparison == comp)|>
    droplevels()
  
  for(sampling_time in unique(pam$time)){
    #first lets understand if there is a difference between treatments
    treat1<-nls(QY ~ Pmin + Pmax * (exp(-alpha*irr/Pmax)),
                data = subset(subset, time == sampling_time & treatment == unique(subset$treatment)[1]),
                start = list(Pmin =  0.06, alpha = 0.001, Pmax =  0.8))
    
    treat2<-nls(QY ~ Pmin + Pmax * (exp(-alpha*irr/Pmax)),
                data = subset(subset, time == sampling_time & treatment == unique(subset$treatment)[2]),
                start = list(Pmin =  0.06, alpha = 0.001, Pmax =  0.8))
    
    # treat2<-nls(QY ~ Pmin[treatment] + Pmax[treatment] * (exp(-alpha[treatment] * irr/Pmax[treatment])),
    #                 data = subset(subset, time == sampling_time, treatment = unique(subset$treatment)[2]),
    #                 start = list(Pmin =  rep(0.06, 2), 
    #                              alpha = rep(0.001, 2), 
    #                              Pmax =  rep(0.8, 2)))
    
    #compare the coefficients of the two models using the function above
    coeffs1 <- data.frame(coef(summary(treat1)))
    coeffs2 <- data.frame(coef(summary(treat2)))
    
    df <- compare_coefs(coeffs1, coeffs2)
    p_value <-df$`p.value`
    
    if (any (p_value > 0.05)) {
      cat("Non-significant result (p =", p_value, ") at", sampling_time, "for", comp,". Adding all `a´s and moving on to next Time.\n")
      psii.cld <- rbind(psii.cld,
                        data.frame(
                          treatment = unique(subset$treatment),
                          comparison = comp,
                          group = rep("a",length(unique(subset$treatment))),
                          time = sampling_time
                        ))
      next
    }
    else{
      cat("Significant ANOVA result (p =", p_value, ") at", sampling_time, ". Continuing loop to look at pairwise comparisions of treatments. \n")
    }
    
    for(treat in unique(subset$treatment)){
      
      #nonlinear least squares approx of the extracted treatment
      treat.nls <- nls(QY ~ Pmin + Pmax * (exp(-alpha*irr/Pmax)),
                       data = subset(subset, 
                                     time == sampling_time & treatment == treat),
                       start = list(Pmin =  0.06, alpha = 0.001, Pmax =  0.8))
      
      #store values of alpha
      psii.alpha <- rbind(psii.alpha, data.frame(
        treatment = treat, 
        comparison = comp,
        alpha = coef(treat.nls)[2],
        low = confint(treat.nls)[2,1],
        high = confint(treat.nls)[2,2],
        time = sampling_time))
      
    }
    psii.overlap <- rbind(psii.overlap,
                          cbind(compare_param(subset(psii.alpha, time == sampling_time)),
                                time = sampling_time))
    dif <- !subset(psii.overlap, time == sampling_time)$overlap
    names <- subset(psii.overlap, time == sampling_time)$pair
    names(dif) <- names
    dif.letters <- multcompLetters(dif)
    
    psii.cld <- rbind(psii.cld,
                      data.frame(
                        treatment = names(dif.letters$Letters),
                        comparison = comp,
                        group = dif.letters$Letters,
                        time = sampling_time
                      ))
    
  }}
```

```{r}
  print(paste("Following analyses are for time", sampling_time))
  
  for(treat in unique(PAM$treatment)){
    #subset data for current treatment + sampling time
    pam.sub <- subset(PAM,
                      treatment == treat & time == sampling_time,
                      select = c(irr, QY))
    
    #fit the model
    print(paste (treat, "at", sampling_time))
    print(head(pam.sub))
    print(paste("Max PSII is:", max(pam.sub$QY), "and min PSII is:", min(pam.sub$QY)))
    fit <- nlsLM(QY ~ SSexpDecay(irr, Pmax, alpha, Pmin),
             data = pam.sub,
             trace = T)
    
    #was this a success?
    if(inherits(fit, "try-error")){
      cat("Better luck next time, error fitting model for", treat, "at", sampling_time, "\n")
      next
    }
    
    #extract parameters
    params <- coef(fit)
    param_estimates <- rbind(param_estimates, 
                             data.frame(treatment = treat, 
                                        Pmax = params["Pmax"], 
                                        alpha = params["alpha"],
                                        Pmin = params["Pmin"]))
    
    #store that summary!
    fit.sum[[paste(treat, sampling_time, sep = "_")]] <- summary(fit)
    
    #store the model!
    all.fit[[paste(treat, sampling_time, sep = "_")]] <- fit
    
    #predictions + confidence intervals
    irradiance_seq <- seq(min(pam.sub$irr), 
                          max(pam.sub$irr),
                          length.out = 100)
    
     # Generate predictions using the fitted model
    pred <- predict2_nls(fit,
                    newdata = data.frame(irr = irradiance_seq),
                    interval = "conf",
                    level = 0.95)

    pred.df<- data.frame(treatment = treat,
                      irr= irradiance_seq, 
                      fit = pred[,1], 
                      lwr = pred[,3], 
                      upr = pred[,4])

    
    # add prediction data to plot list
    plot.list[[treat]] <- pred.df
  }
  
  #what about comparing these models?

  #combine all predictions for current sampling time
  combined_pred <- do.call(rbind, plot.list) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment))
  
  #getting 95% confidence interval to plot "ranges" for each Irradiance/Treatment
  ci.point <- summarySE(data = subset(PAM, time == sampling_time),
                        "QY",

    mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment))
  
  #plooooot! note: this is for one sampling time at a time
  p <- ggplot()+
    geom_errorbar(data = ci.point,

                      color = treatment),

                              position = position_dodge(150))+  # 95% confidence error bars
    geom_point(data = ci.point,
               aes(x= irr, y = QY, color = treatment),
               position = position_dodge(150))+

                aes(x=irr, ymin =lwr, ymax=upr, fill= treatment),
                alpha = 0.2)+

    # annotate(geom = "text", x= 3500, y = 0.525, label = subset(psii.cld, time == sampling_time & treatment == 60)$group)+
    labs(title = paste("Chlorophyll Fluorescence at", sampling_time),

}
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false

## Y(NO) [fluorescence + dissipated heat]= Y(FD) ----
#the sum of the fluorescence and constitive heat dissipation  (i.e. 1 - (Y(PSII) + Y(NPQ)))

## We cannot compare this data using a clean logistic model because of the expected peak
## at 100 umol Irradiance. Thus we have to compare the values of the peaks + the 
## values of the saturation levels.

#finding significances
#for Y(NO) this is looking at the "peak" and saturation values - 
#i.e. normal anova comparisons (as long as the data is normally distributed)

yno.values <- pam %>% 
  dplyr::select(Irradiance, YNO, Time, Treatment) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Irradiance==100 | Irradiance == 4500) %>%
  dplyr:: summarise(.by = c(Time, Irradiance, Treatment), value = mean(YNO)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Irradiance, values_from = value) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(peak = `100`, saturation = `4500`)

for(irr in c("100", "4500")){
  if(irr == "100"){
    temp.group<-data.frame(Treatment = factor(),
                           Time = character(),
                           peak.group = character())
  }else{
    temp.group <- data.frame(Treatment = factor(),
                             Time = character(),
                             sat.group = character())
  }
  for(sampling_time in unique(pam$Time)){
    
    sub<-subset(pam, Time == sampling_time & Irradiance == as.numeric(irr))
    
    cat("Looking at the values at", sampling_time, "for irradiance =", irr,"\n")

    #check if data is normally distributed
    norm<-shapiro.test(sub$YNO)
    
    if(norm$p.value > 0.05){
      cat("The data is normally distributed, go on. \n")
      
      #perform tukey post hoc on data
      hsd <-HSD.test(aov(YNO~Treatment, data = sub), "Treatment", group = T)
      print(hsd$groups)
      
      sub.group <- subset(rownames_to_column(hsd$groups, "Treatment"),
                          select = c(Treatment, groups))
      group.name<- colnames(temp.group)[3]
      
      #store data in `temp.group` dataframe
      temp.group <- rbind(temp.group,
                          data.frame(Treatment = sub.group$Treatment,
                                     Time = sampling_time,
                                     groups = sub.group$groups) %>% 
                            dplyr::rename(!!group.name := groups))
      
    }else{
      cat("The data is not normally distributed. How can we transform it? \n")
      
      loglike<-boxcox(YNO~Treatment, data = sub, plotit = F) #saves boxcox power transformation log-likelyhoods
      trans<-loglike$x[which(loglike$y == max(loglike$y))]   #extracts the lambda vector (i.e. transformation) for the highest likelyhood (of normality)
      cat("We need to use a", trans , "power transformation to have a normally distributed dataset. 
        The following analyses will be done with said transformation on the data.\n")
      
      norm2<-shapiro.test(sub$YNO^trans)
      if(norm2$p.value > 0.05){
        cat("We now have a normally distributed (transformed) dataset. \n")
        
        #perform tukey post hoc on transformed data
        hsd <-HSD.test(aov(YNO^trans~Treatment, data = sub), "Treatment", group = T)
        print(hsd$groups)
        
        
        sub.group <- subset(rownames_to_column(hsd$groups, "Treatment"),
                            select = c(Treatment, groups))
        group.name<- colnames(temp.group)[3]
        
        #store data in `temp.group` dataframe
        temp.group <- rbind(temp.group,
                            data.frame(Treatment = sub.group$Treatment,
                                       Time = sampling_time,
                                       groups = sub.group$groups) %>% 
                              dplyr::rename(!!group.name := groups))
        
      }else{
        cat("Be sad")
        break
      }
    }
  }
  yno.values<-yno.values %>% 
    left_join(temp.group)
}

##Non-photochemical Quenching Y(NPQ)----
## We can look at this data using  a asymptotic model (yay!).

#summarize the data by treatment/irradiance using function established at the beginning of code
ynpq.sum <- summarySE(data = pam, "YNPQ", groupvars = c("Treatment", "Irradiance"))

#plot that summary!

ggplot(ynpq.sum, aes(x=Irradiance, y=YNPQ, colour = Treatment))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = YNPQ-ci, ymax = YNPQ+ci), 
                width = 0.1, 
                position = position_dodge(150))+  # 95% confidence error bars
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(150))


#####
# Note: If we compare estimates of the same coeffs from samples of different 
# populations, we can indicate statistical significance if CIs don't overlap, 
# but not robustly say that there is no difference if they do.
#####

#looking at some significance

#A Note: We cannot compare individual models pairwise with an ANOVA as it abuses
#the assumption of the F-test that they are nested and fitted to the same data.
#THUS we will compare the model fitted to the _whole_ data set compared to the
#same model fitted for each group to see if there is a statistical difference
#between groups. If this returns positive, we will look at the alpha parameter
#individually - the one defining the shape of the curve, using the CI interval
#generated by nls().

#convert treatments to factors
pam.factor <- pam %>% mutate(Treatment = as.factor(Treatment))

#create frames to fill in for loop with ci overlaps
ynpq.overlap <- data.frame(pair = character(),
                           overlap = logical(),
                           time = character())

ynpq.cld <- data.frame(treatment = character(),
                       letter = character(),
                       time = character())


#initiate data frame to store parameter value and confidence intervals
ynpq.lrc <- data.frame(treatment = character(),
                       est = numeric(),
                       low = numeric(),
                       high = numeric(),
                       time = character(),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


for(sampling_time in unique(pam$Time)){
  #first lets understand if there is a difference between treatments
  no.treats<-nls(YNPQ ~ Asym*(1 - exp(-exp(lrc)*Irradiance)),
                 data = subset(pam.factor, Time == sampling_time),
                 start = list(Asym =  max(pam.factor$YNPQ), lrc = -6.17))
  
  all.treats<-nls(YNPQ ~ Asym[Treatment]*(1 - exp(-exp(lrc[Treatment])*Irradiance)),
                  data = subset(pam.factor, Time == sampling_time),
                  start = list(Asym =  rep(max(pam.factor$YNPQ), 2), 
                               lrc = rep(-6.17, 2)))
  
  time.anova<- anova(no.treats, all.treats)
  p_value <- time.anova$`Pr(>F)`[2]
  
  if (p_value > 0.05) {
    cat("Non-significant ANOVA result (p =", p_value, ") at", sampling_time, ". Adding `a´s and moving to next Time.\n")
    ynpq.cld <- rbind(ynpq.cld,
                      data.frame(
                        treatment = unique(pam$Treatment),
                        group = rep("a",length(unique(pam$Treatment))),
                        time = sampling_time
                      ))
    next
  }
  else{
    cat("Significant ANOVA result (p =", p_value, ") at", sampling_time, ". Continuing loop to look at pairwise comparisions of treatments. \n")
  }

  for(treat in unique(pam$Treatment)){
    
    #nonlinear least squares approx of the extracted treatment
    treat.nls <- nls(YNPQ ~ Asym*(1 - exp(-exp(lrc)*Irradiance)),
                     data = subset(pam.factor, 
                                   Time == sampling_time & Treatment == treat),
                     start = list(Asym =  max(pam.factor$YNPQ), lrc = -6.17))
    
    #store values of alpha
    ynpq.lrc <- rbind(ynpq.lrc, data.frame(
      treatment = treat, 
      lrc = coef(treat.nls)[2],
      low = confint(treat.nls)[2,1],
      high = confint(treat.nls)[2,2],
      time = sampling_time))
    
  }
  ynpq.overlap <- rbind(ynpq.overlap,
                        cbind(compare_param(ynpq.lrc),
                              time = sampling_time))
  dif <- !subset(ynpq.overlap, time == sampling_time)$overlap
  names <- subset(ynpq.overlap, time == sampling_time)$pair
  names(dif) <- names
  dif.letters <- multcompLetters(dif)
  
  ynpq.cld <- rbind(ynpq.cld,
                    data.frame(
                      treatment = names(dif.letters$Letters),
                      group = dif.letters$Letters,
                      time = sampling_time
                    ))
  
}
```

```{r}
#| label: photosynthesis data cleaning
```

### Leaf temperature

```{r}
#| label: leaf temp

#test for normality
shapiro.test(walz$Tleaf) 
#p-value = 0.052, so the data is (barely) normally distributed and we can use
#parametric tests for our statistics

      ifelse(shapiro.test(walz$Tleaf)$p.value > 0.05, "non-significant,", "significant,"), 
      "the data is", 
      ifelse(shapiro.test(walz$Tleaf)$p.value > 0.05, "normally distributed \n and we will use t-test for comparison going forward.", 
             "non-normally distributed \n and we will use the Wilcox test for comparison going forward.")))

#base facet plot

tleaf.plot<-
  walz.comp |>
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = Tleaf, fill = treatment))+
  geom_boxplot(data = walz, color = "grey",fill = "grey")+ 
  geom_boxplot()+
  geom_jitter(width=0.01)+
  labs(title = "Leaf Temperature",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Temperature °C")+

                     label = "p.signif",
                     #label.y = 3.05,

  )+

                     label = "p.format",
                     label.y.npc = "bottom"
  )+
  facet_grid(~comparison, drop = TRUE)+
  #ylim(NA, 3.1)+
  theme_bw( )+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),

        legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
  geom_jitter(width=0.01)+
```

```{r}
      ifelse(shapiro.test(biometric$diameter)$p.value > 0.05, "non-significant,", "significant,"), 
      "the data is", 
      ifelse(shapiro.test(biometric$diameter)$p.value > 0.05, "normally distributed \n and we will use t-test for comparison going forward.", 
             "non-normally distributed \n and we will use the Wilcox test for comparison going forward.")))

diam.plot<- 
  biometric.comp |>
  dplyr::filter(drought == "nd")|>
  ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = diameter, fill = treatment))+
  geom_boxplot(data = biometric|> filter(drought == "nd"), color = "grey",fill = "grey")+ 
  geom_boxplot()+
  geom_jitter(width=0.01)+
  labs(title = "Rosette Diameter",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Diameter (mm)")+
  scale_fill_manual(values= cols)+
  stat_compare_means(method = method3, 
                     label = "p.signif",
                     #label.y = 22,
                     label.x.npc = c(0.3, 0.2, 0.75, 0.6)
  )+
  stat_compare_means(method = method3, 
                     label = "p.format",
                     label.y.npc = "bottom"
  )+
  facet_grid(time~comparison, drop = TRUE)+
  #ylim(0, 25)+
  theme_bw( )+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "bottom")

diam.plot

#ggsave("leafnum.plot.png",leafnum.plot)
```

```{r}
shapiro.test(beakers$`evap rate (mm/hr)`)
```
